title: Section 2: Test
competency: The learner coordinates with other professionals and families of students with exceptionalities to foster advocacy, facilitate connection with available resources, and promote culturally responsive communication.

questions.prompt: Which strategy should a teacher use to inform parents of their rights as part of the IEP process?
options: Call the parents and explain to them the parental rights and responsibilities.
Have the principal of the school take responsibility for sharing parental rights and responsibilities.
Send parents an email with a detailed description of parental rights and responsibilities.
Provide parents with a written copy of parental rights and responsibilities during every meeting and be sure the parents understand the information being presented.
questions.why: Providing a written copy must be accompanied by conversation so parents understand their rights and responsibilities.
questions.note: WGU's best-practice answer says 'every meeting'; the general legal requirement for providing safeguards notices is more nuanced. Teach the answer as the course's preferred inclusive practice, not an absolute legal frequency.

questions.prompt: Which strategy can effectively help parents understand assessment results?
options: Allowing the parents to silently read the assessment results at the PPT meeting and wait for them to ask questions
Providing feedback and assessment results in a private, comfortable setting and using language that is free of jargon while allowing time for questions or concerns throughout your meeting
Providing a website or online link that explains generic assessment results
Providing the written assessment results and telling them to call or email you with questions
questions.why: A private discussion using plain language and pauses for questions gives parents information they can use in educational decisions.

questions.prompt: Which statement best illustrates the importance of collaboration in student-centered teams?
options: Inclusive practices in collaboration mean that only the needs of the students are prioritized, leaving educators' needs unaddressed.
Collaboration allows for individual accountability, ensuring that each member can work independently without considering others’ contributions.
Effective communication in teams enables members to analyze data together, leading to decisions based on shared facts and evidence.
Collaboration restricts goal setting to a single leader, preventing confusion about team objectives.
questions.why: Communicating and examining evidence together allows the team to make shared, data-informed decisions.

questions.prompt: Which is an effective strategy for overcoming collaboration challenges with general education teachers?
options: Keep students’ well-being and success at the forefront of collaborative efforts.
Accepting that there are differences of opinion and working separately.
Focusing on the credentials of the special educator and the general educator.
Using a paraprofessional as a mediator when disagreements arise.
questions.why: A student-centered focus helps general and special educators work toward a shared purpose.

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the importance of culturally responsive practices in educational settings?
options: Teachers should only focus on their own cultural background when planning lessons.
Involving families in decision-making is less important than meeting academic standards.
Building good relationships and understanding cultural differences among team members enhances collaboration and improves educational outcomes for all students.
Culturally responsive practices are mainly about incorporating diverse teaching materials.
questions.why: Cultural understanding and strong relationships support teamwork and positive outcomes.

questions.prompt: What is an effective way to create a welcoming environment in advance of an IEP meeting?
options: Email the parents a list of concerns regarding the students' progress.
Send the parents a list of things they can and cannot ask during the IEP meeting to make sure the meeting time is used effectively.
Prepare parents by sending agendas and potential questions in advance and arranging informal interactions before the IEP meeting.
Call the parents to discuss specific categories of disability and which category the student will likely fall under to prepare the parents for the meeting.
questions.why: Advance agendas, sample questions, and informal contact help parents arrive feeling prepared, respected and welcome.

questions.prompt: At the start of the meeting, why is it important to explain the interpreter's commitment to confidentiality to parents?
options: Avoids legal issues
Reduces hesitation in sharing sensitive information
Allows parents to know the translator is a professional
Keeps the meeting flowing at a steady pace
questions.why: Explaining interpreter confidentiality can reassure parents that sensitive information will remain private and encourage them to speak openly.
